title: Irreducible refinement of a finite stratification
statement: For a Noetherian scheme X and finite stratification S, there exists a finite stratification T refining S whose strata are irreducible.

source.place: (1)-(3); scheme version Tag 0BA8; finite-component disjointification as detailed in the docstring

proof.text: On each stratum use the Noetherian topology induced by its immersion. Mathlib TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.finite_irreducibleComponents enumerates its components. Subtract earlier components; closure_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff_singleton and IsPreirreducible.subset_irreducible show every remainder is nonempty and irreducible. Least indices give coverage and ordering gives disjointness. Realize each locally closed remainder by the vanishing-ideal closed subscheme of its coborder open subscheme, using IdealSheafData.range_subschemeι. Compose with the original immersion, and reindex the finite dependent sum by Fin. Embedding injectivity proves within-stratum disjointness, and the original partition proves cross-stratum disjointness. Local closedness implies constructibility in Noetherian X. This uses the general topological Mathlib theorem directly, rather than the scheme-level finite-components node.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_irreducible_refinement_topological
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (S : Stratification X) :
    ∃ T : Stratification X,
      T.Refines S ∧ ∀ i : Fin T.n, IrreducibleSpace (T.domain i)
